test_title: PYST 56: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Why do aquatic organisms breathe faster than terrestrial organisms?

options.text: Because they absorb oxygen directly from sunlight through gills
Because diffusion of oxygen in water is faster than in air
Because the amount of dissolved oxygen in water is very low
Because water exerts less resistance on breathing organs

solution:
The correct answer is __**Because the amount of dissolved oxygen in water is very low**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aquatic organisms**, such as **fish**, **prawns**, and **mollusks**, obtain the **oxygen** necessary for **respiration** from the **oxygen dissolved in water**.
 
• The concentration of **oxygen** in the **atmosphere** is approximately **21%**, whereas the amount of **dissolved oxygen** in **water** is significantly lower (roughly **0.7%** or **4 to 10 milligrams per liter** depending on conditions).
 
• Because the **oxygen level** is so low in **aquatic environments**, these organisms must take in water more frequently and pass it over their **respiratory organs** (like **gills**) to extract enough **oxygen** to meet their **metabolic demands**.
 
• This necessity results in a much **faster breathing rate** in **aquatic animals** compared to **terrestrial animals**, who have access to an abundant and concentrated supply of **atmospheric oxygen**.
 
• In **fish**, water is taken in through the **mouth** and forced past the **gills**, where the **dissolved oxygen** is absorbed into the **bloodstream** by **diffusion** across thin membranes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxygen Solubility:** The **solubility of oxygen** in water is affected by **temperature**; **cold water** can hold more **dissolved oxygen** than **warm water**. Consequently, **aquatic life** may struggle more in **higher temperatures** due to **hypoxia**.
 
• **Gills:** These are specialized **respiratory structures** in **aquatic organisms** that provide a large **surface area** for **gas exchange**. They are highly **vascularized** to facilitate the efficient transfer of **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide**.
 
• **Lungs vs. Gills:** While **terrestrial organisms** use **lungs** to breathe **air**, **gills** are adapted specifically for **aqueous environments**. **Gills** would collapse and dry out in **air**, making them ineffective for **terrestrial respiration**.
 
• **Diffusion Rate:** The **diffusion** of **oxygen** in **air** is nearly **10,000 times faster** than its **diffusion** in **water**. This physical limitation forces **aquatic animals** to evolve highly efficient mechanisms to extract **oxygen**.
 
• **Viscosity of Water:** **Water** is about **800 times denser** and much more **viscous** than **air**. This means **aquatic organisms** expend significantly more **energy** to move the medium (water) over their **respiratory surfaces** than **terrestrial animals** do with **air**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Counter-Current Exchange:** Most **fish** utilize a **counter-current flow** mechanism where **blood** flows in the opposite direction to the **water** passing over the **gills**. This maintains a **concentration gradient** that allows them to extract up to **80-90%** of the **dissolved oxygen**.
 
• **Metabolic Rate:** Despite the **faster breathing rate**, many **aquatic organisms** have a lower **metabolic rate** compared to **endothermic** (warm-blooded) **terrestrial mammals** because they do not need to generate **internal body heat**.
 
• **Environmental Factors:** Factors such as **salinity**, **pollution**, and **depth** also influence the **dissolved oxygen** levels. For instance, **saltwater** typically holds less **oxygen** than **freshwater** at the same **temperature**.
 
• **Evolutionary Adaptation:** The **high breathing rate** is an **evolutionary adaptation** to ensure survival in an **oxygen-poor** medium, highlighting the **biological diversity** in **respiratory strategies** across different **habitats**.
</ul
